INELIGIBLE TO ACQUIRE FEDERAL ONSHORE OIL AND GAS LEASE UNDER THE MINERAL LEASING ACT (30 USC 181 ET SEQ.).  Pursuant to section 17(g) of the Mineral Leasing Act (30 USC 226(g)), the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) is prohibited from issuing an oil and gas lease, or approving an assignment or transfer of a lease, to an entity that has failed or refused to comply in any material respect with the reclamation requirements and other standards established under that section.  Prior to making such a determination, the BLM must provide the entity with adequate notification and an opportunity to comply.  This entity is in noncompliance with section 17(g) and has been afforded the requisite notice and opportunity to comply.  THIS EXCLUSION APPLIES ONLY TO FEDERAL ONSHORE OIL AND GAS LEASES ISSUED BY THE BUREAU OF LAND MANAGEMENT, DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR.

Debarment was proposed because an investigation by the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) Office of Inspector General (OIG) revealed that between 2018 and 2021, LYNCH LIVESTOCK, INC. managers and employees directed and participated in a fraudulent scheme to manipulate scales, re-classify hogs, and falsify records to pay livestock producers less than fair market value for their hogs. The OIG investigation uncovered a pattern of fraudulent practices by LYNCH LIVESTOCK, INC.:
Scale Manipulation: LYNCH LIVESTOCK, INC.’s employees manipulated hog scales at the buying stations at the direction of their managers. The employees used a crowbar to decrease the weight of the hogs on the scale so that the producers would be paid less.
Falsified Records: LYNCH LIVESTOCK, INC.’s managers created fraudulent scale tickets and sort sheets to conceal their scheme. The original sort sheets and scale tickets, which contained the actual weights and classifications of the hogs, were routinely destroyed.
Hog Classification: LYNCH LIVESTOCK, INC.’s employees, acting on instructions from managers, intentionally downgraded hog classifications. They would classify hogs as being of a lower quality than they were, which allowed LYNCH LIVESTOCK, INC. to pay the producers less for their hogs. TYLER THOMS stated that he and another employee were responsible for shredding the original sort sheets at the direction of their managers.

For further information contact the U.S. Department of Agriculture Agency Exclusions POC.

INELIGIBLE TO ACQUIRE FEDERAL ONSHORE OIL AND GAS LEASE UNDER THE MINERAL LEASING ACT (30 USC 181 ET SEQ.).  Pursuant to section 17(g) of the Mineral Leasing Act (30 USC 226(g)), the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) is prohibited from issuing an oil and gas lease, or approving an assignment or transfer of a lease, to an entity that has failed or refused to comply in any material respect with the reclamation requirements and other standards established under that section.  Prior to making such a determination, the BLM must provide the entity with adequate notification and an opportunity to comply.  This entity is in noncompliance with section 17(g) and has been afforded the requisite notice and opportunity to comply.  THIS EXCLUSION APPLIES ONLY TO FEDERAL ONSHORE OIL AND GAS LEASES ISSUED BY THE BUREAU OF LAND MANAGEMENT, DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR.

The Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. 7606) forbids any Federal agency from entering into any contract, loan, or benefit to any person or company who- 1. Has been convicted of an offense under the Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. 7413(c)); AND 2. Owns, leases or supervises the facility (where or from which the Clean Air Act offense occurred) at the time when a decision about the contract, loan or benefit is made.  ALL THREE CONDITIONS MUST BE PRESENT FOR A PERSON TO BE DENIED A CONTRACT, LOAN OR BENEFIT.

INELIGIBLE TO ACQUIRE FEDERAL ONSHORE OIL AND GAS LEASE UNDER THE MINERAL LEASING ACT (30 USC 181 ET SEQ.).  Pursuant to section 17(g) of the Mineral Leasing Act (30 USC 226(g)), the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) is prohibited from issuing an oil and gas lease, or approving an assignment or transfer of a lease, to an entity that has failed or refused to comply in any material respect with the reclamation requirements and other standards established under that section.  Prior to making such a determination, the BLM must provide the entity with adequate notification and an opportunity to comply.  This entity is in noncompliance with section 17(g) and has been afforded the requisite notice and opportunity to comply.  THIS EXCLUSION APPLIES ONLY TO FEDERAL ONSHORE OIL AND GAS LEASES ISSUED BY THE BUREAU OF LAND MANAGEMENT, DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR.

Has been convicted of an offense under the Clean Water Act (33 U.S.C. 1319(c)); AND 2. Intends to use the place where or from which the offense happened (the violating facility) for the contract, loan or benefit; AND 3. Owns, leases or supervises the facility (where or from which the Clean Water Act offense occurred) at the time when a decision about the contract, loan or benefit is made. ALL THREE CONDITIONS MUST BE PRESENT FOR A PERSON TO BE DENIED A CONTRACT, LOAN OR BENEFIT.

Debarment was proposed because a USDA Office of Inspector General
(OIG) investigation revealed that CAPELLAN, DIAZ, and GUILIANO
engaged in a scheme whereby they purchased produce on credit from
growers for resale but failed to remit payment.
When growers and/or shipping companies pursued payment through email and/or phone and text messages, CAPELLAN, DIAZ, and
GUILIANO ceased all communication. After a certain amount of time
and claims made against a certain company name, CAPELLAN, DIAZ,
and GUILIANO would “close” that company and open a new company
under a new and “clean” name.
As a result of the scheme, victims lost more than $973,000 in unpaid
produce and shipping orders. For further information contact the U.S. Department of Agriculture Agency Exclusions POC.

The Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. 7606) forbids any Federal agency from entering into any contract, loan, or benefit to any person or company who- 1. Has been convicted of an offense under the Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. 7413(c)); AND 2. Intends to use the place where or from which the offense happened (the violating facility) for the contract, loan or benefit; AND 3. Owns, leases or supervises the facility (where or from which the Clean Air Act offense occurred) at the time when a decision about the contract, loan or benefit is made. ALL THREE CONDITIONS MUST BE PRESENT FOR A PERSON TO BE DENIED A CONTRACT, LOAN OR BENEFIT.
